newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan share prices seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan share prices seen consolidating.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to consolidate on Tuesday with investors likely to remain on the sidelines, despite Wall Street's overnight gains, brokers said.
On Monday, the weighted index closed up 45.24 points, or 0.54 percent, at 8,269.43.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 143.29 points, or 2.03 percent, to 7,214.49, beating the old mark of 7,085.16 set on March 11 and its 16th record so far this year.
Wall Street's overnight rise was unlikely to have a significant boost to the market, brokers said.
"The Wall Street movements will only influence our market when sentiment is extremely optimistic or pessmistic," said Oliver Fang, an analyst of National Securities.
"I don't think people will use this as an excuse today. The market's trend is still unclear and people don't know what to buy," Fang said.

Brokers said electronic shares, especially semiconductor counters, might face selling pressure after a 20-minute power outage in Taiwan's Hsinchu Science-based Industrial Park on Monday shut down operations at many electronic firms.
Some manufacturers estimated losses would total around T$1 billion.
A range of 8,200-8,300 was seen for Tuesday.
